- [x] I checked and didn't find similar issue

### 🏢 Have you read the Code of Conduct?

- [x] I have read the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/appwrite/appwrite/blob/HEAD/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)
comments:
I can reproduce this on `appwrite: 21.4.0` with Appwrite server `1.8.1` during realtime card moves.

  Root cause:
  `RealtimeMessage.fromMap` assumes `events/channels/subscriptions` are always `List`, but some realtime packets come
  through as `Map`.
  That causes:
  `type '_Map<String, dynamic>' is not a subtype of type 'Iterable<dynamic>'`.

  Temporary fix (works for me):
  Patch Flutter SDK realtime parsing to accept both `List` and `Map` shapes.

  ### 1) `lib/src/realtime_message.dart`
  - Parse `events` and `channels` from either `List` or `Map.values`
  - Parse `payload` safely from `Map`

  ### 2) `lib/src/realtime_mixin.dart` (event case)
  - Guard `if (data.data is! Map) break;`
  - Parse `subscriptions` from either `List` or `Map.values`

  After this patch, realtime crash disappears. I actually noticed this on my web app, but was able to properly diagnose it when debugging natively.

Gonna be watching for a fix if someone takes it up, but my suggestions are valid I think. I patched those two files locally and bootstrapped them into my app for now.

title: Silent special-cast failures — add HUD feedback (especially during TIME STOP)
body:
THIS MESSAGE WAS GENERATED BY AN AUTOMATED PROCESS

### Observed

During a mage TIME STOP in the playtest, another player's special "didn't
work" with zero feedback; players concluded "when time is stopped we can only
run and hit."

### Findings (classic behavior — investigated)

Classic Gladiator did not explicitly bar specials during the freeze. The
heritage trail (`docs/glad.txt:575-576, 686`) only records that generators
stop during "NULL-TIME"; nothing in glad.txt/scen.txt/help_classes.txt blocks
specials, and the port has no input gate on `enemy_freeze`
(`src/gameplay/sim_input_handler.cpp:346-359` still dispatches
`control->special()`). The observed lockout is three silent mechanisms:

1. **MP regen halts for everyone during the freeze**
   (`src/gameplay/living.cpp:152-160` → `compute_regen_tick` no-ops when
   frozen) — so a drained caster stays drained for the whole stop.
2. **Insufficient MP fails with no cue** — `walker_specials.cpp:160-162`
   returns 0 with no sound/notification (likewise `:132` `specials_disabled()`).
3. **Players on a non-`my_team` alliance are act-frozen** — their `living::act`
   never runs, so command-queue specials (soldier rush, archer volley, thief)
   silently never execute, while movement/fire keep working because the input
   handler calls `walkstep()`/`init_fire()` directly (`:363-377`).

### Proposed fix

- Give `walker::special()` a failure-reason out-param
  (`walker_specials.cpp:126-165`: NoMP / Disabled / Frozen / NotLiving).
- In the sim input handler (player casts only — never inside
  `walker::special()`, which AI also calls), emit feedback on failure using the
  existing "Yo!" pattern (`sim_input_handler.cpp:262-266`): e.g.
  `"NOT ENOUGH MP"`, `"SPECIALS FROZEN"` + a buzz sound.
  `viewscreen::refresh_display_text` already dedupes repeated lines.
- Same gap one screen up: a personally-frozen player (faerie/orc stun) has all
  input dropped with zero feedback (`sim_input_handler.cpp:328-334`) — cover it
  in the same pass.
- Note: notifications are broadcast to all views today (`screen.cpp:243-251`,
  no player field on `og::sim::Event`). Fine for a first pass; per-seat
  addressing is a separate enhancement.

### Tests

Unit: special with insufficient MP returns reason NoMP; integration: failed
player cast during `enemy_freeze` produces the notification event
(pattern: `tests/integration/test_runtime_coverage_paths.cpp:1562-1575`).

title: Fighter/team switching fails silently when there's no valid target
body:
THIS MESSAGE WAS GENERATED BY AN AUTOMATED PROCESS

### Observed

Playtest: switching toward the blue team (not present in the level — see #218) did nothing, with no message — the switch requests were silently ignored
and nobody could tell why.

### Root cause

All four switch paths are silent no-ops on failure:

1. **SwitchChar cycle** — `sim_input_handler.cpp:197-199`: `if (!control)
   control = oldcontrol;` — no sound, no toast.
2. **Cheat team-cycle** — `src/interface/cheat_handler.cpp:35-76`: wraps back
   silently; plus two latent bugs: `world_.my_team` is written
   unconditionally *before* the null check (a failed cycle can move the
   alliance that freeze/completion logic reads), and the scan doesn't test
   `dead()`/`dormant()` — it can hand control to a corpse.
3. **Spectator camera cycle** — `view.cpp:1389-1410`: silent when empty.
4. **Networked follow cycle** — `local_transport_shadow.cpp:1524-1566` returns
   false; discarded at `view.cpp:1383-1385`.

The lobby already does this right: `base_camp_cycle_seat_team` pops
"CHANGE DENIED" and only offers authored teams
(`src/interface/ui/menu_screen_specs.cpp:2687-2712`).

### Proposed fix

- Emit feedback on each failed path — in-sim paths via the event log
  ("NO ONE TO SWITCH TO"; team cycle: `og::sim::team_color_name` for
  "BLUE TEAM NOT IN LEVEL"), render-side paths via
  `screen::do_notify(msg, who)` which targets the requesting view.
- Fix the cheat handler: restore `my_team` on failure; filter dead/dormant like
  `sim_input_handler.cpp:191` does.

### Tests

Unit-level for the cheat handler ordering; integration: SwitchChar with no
eligible teammate emits the notification.

title: Engine: detached camera viewscreens, creatable and centered from Lua
body:
THIS MESSAGE WAS GENERATED BY AN AUTOMATED PROCESS

### Summary

Modes need a viewscreen that isn't a player seat: a camera that follows an
arbitrary walker (first consumer: the ball in Soccer/Basketball — see the
application section below).
Wanted: engine-owned "camera view" support plus a small Lua surface to create,
target, and destroy such views.

### What exists

- `MAX_VIEWS == 5` already leaves one spare slot past the 4-player cap
  (`include/openglad/interface/screen.h:48,403`).
- The demo "Boss camera" is the proven half of this: point `view->control` at
  a non-player walker, set `following_ = true`, and HUD/radar stay quiet
  (`src/platform/sdl/demo.cpp:227-263`, gates at `view.cpp:946-950`,
  `score_panel.cpp:653`).
- `viewscreen::resize(x,y,w,h)` direct-geometry path exists for editor/capture
  cameras (`view.cpp:1802`).
- The beacon precedent shows how Lua-driven presentation state stays
  deterministic and mirror-safe: it lives in `og::sim::ModeState` and is
  replicated in snapshot v10 (`mode_state.h:44-64`). A camera request should
  ride the same channel (e.g. a `camera_target` beacon-like slot), with the
  interface layer materializing/destroying the actual viewscreen.

### What has to change

1. **A view kind.** `viewob[]` entries need a player-seat vs camera
   distinction. Every per-frame loop currently treats all views as seats:
   input dispatch (`screen.cpp:1444-1465` and `viewscreen::process_input`
   `view.cpp:1359` — unchecked `players[mynum]`, OOB for `mynum == 4`),
   `do_notify`, panel chrome, results classification
   (`results_screen.cpp:112-121` would count a ball camera as a loser team),
   seat claiming (`glad_gameplay.cpp:171-225`, `game.cpp:283-312`), pause-menu
   `seat_view`, and the network shadow's `compute_local_player_count` /
   `add_local_player` (`local_transport_shadow.cpp:482-491, 1830-1922`).
   Camera views must be skipped by all seat logic.
2. **Layout.** `compute_view_layout` keys on `numviews`; camera views need
   either (a) participation in layout (3 players + ball cam → the existing
   4-quadrant `default:` arm — desired for the ball camera below) or (b) an explicit
   overlay rect via the direct-geometry resize (1/2/4-player center inset).
   Suggest: layout participation count = seats + docked cameras; overlay
   cameras bypass layout entirely. Guard the `numviews`-keyed HUD rules
   (`score_panel.cpp:760`, `radar.cpp:261`, border suppression
   `screen.cpp:1725-1727`) to count seats, not views.
3. **Per-view prefs bounds.** `options::load` and HUD-settings I/O guard
   `mynum >= 4`; camera views need sane defaults (currently `prefs[10]` is
   uninitialized for out-of-range seats, `view.h:237`).
4. **Camera field.** Reuse `control` + `following_` (liveness enforced by
   `sanitize_control_pointer`, `view.cpp:168-174`). A control-less positional
   camera would need per-view topx/topy (today the free camera is
   screen-global, `view.cpp:711-716`) — defer; entity-following suffices for
   the ball.

### Proposed Lua API (via ModeState, deterministic)

```lua
og.set_camera_view(slot, entity_or_nil [, opts])
-- opts.style = "docked" (join the split layout) | "inset" (centered overlay)
-- nil target destroys the view
```

Interface layer watches the replicated slot each frame (like beacons) and
creates/retargets/destroys the viewscreen accordingly — works on netplay
mirrors and in replays for free.

### First application: ball camera in Soccer/Basketball

The motivating consumer (from the idea recordings): always give players a view
of the ball.

- **3 local players:** instead of today's "one large + two small" layout, run
  four equal quadrants — three player views plus a fourth, ball-following
  camera view slotted in as if it were another player. Convenient: 4 views
  already produce the quadrant layout via the `default:` arm
  (`view_layout.h:142-152`).
- **1, 2, or 4 local players:** no spare quadrant — Lua pops a small inset
  viewscreen centered on the screen showing just the immediate area around
  the ball.

Mode-side sketch: in `mode_soccer_impl.lua` / `mode_basketball_impl.lua` init
(and on kickoff/ball respawn): `og.set_camera_view(0, ball, {style = seats ==
3 and "docked" or "inset"})`. The seat count needs exposing to Lua (e.g.
`og.match_setting("local_seats")`) or the docked/inset choice stays
engine-side policy. Entity-follow handles `kickoff_reset` teleports; hide the
view during intermissions. Keep the existing beacon (`og.set_beacon(0, ball)`)
— minimap/arrow and live view are complementary.

Application-level open questions:

- Inset size/position: suggest ~1/4 pane centered, borderless, above HUD
  chrome but below pause UI.
- Should the inset be toggleable per player (pause menu), given it covers
  world pixels?
- Curses/headless backends: no-op the camera view where
  `world_present_partition_supported()` is false (same fence per-view zoom
  uses, `view.cpp:1882-1890`).

### Tests

`test_view_layout.cpp` (add expected arms), `test_game_loop.cpp:890-894`
currently pins "no extra views" — update; new integration test: camera view
created/destroyed via mode var, input isolation (camera view consumes no
player input), HUD/radar quiet on camera views.

title: Design: "Office" — knowledge-worker economy mode
body:
THIS MESSAGE WAS GENERATED BY AN AUTOMATED PROCESS

### Pitch (from the idea recording, refined)

Teams of knowledge workers earn money by doing work at computers; finishing
your own work licenses you to raid the other teams to stop theirs.

### Design stance

Office is normal OpenGlad with a twist — ordinary classes, combat, death, and
corpses; the only changes are the objective (money from work) and when you're
allowed to fight. The `modes.core` toolkit (mode registration,
level band, `mode_match` census/FAIR activation, HUD lines, `og.award_score`,
win check) is just plumbing: mode #8, `MODE = { ... OFFICE=8 }`.

**Work loop.** Desks are anchors. A worker at their own team's desk "works"
by channeling: stand adjacent + hold the fire input; presence advances a
per-desk progress var (ModeState vars, like `S.GOALS`). A completed work unit
pays `og.award_score(team, T.work_value)` — money is per-team — and rings
a cash sound. The recorded "30 vs 45 button presses" debate becomes tuning:
`T.presses_per_unit` as the duration knob.

**The license-to-attack rule.** You can deal damage when either (a) you've
completed your current work unit — armed until the next unit starts — or (b)
you're standing in your own team's office wing (home turf), so a pacifist
team can always defend itself. Implemented as an `on_damage` hook zeroing
attacker damage when neither condition holds. Bots run the same loop
(worker/raider/defender roles per squad).

**Death and revival.** The fighter dies normally and leaves a normal corpse
(the stain; issue #221's corpse persistence is the prerequisite). Two revival
paths:

1. **Cleric resurrect** — already works today on stains
   (`packs/core/families/living-05-cleric.lua:217-260`); nothing new needed.
2. **Coffee delivery** — coffee machine anchors dispense a carryable coffee
   item (treasure family `modes:coffee`; the CTF flag-carry machinery is the
   precedent); bringing it to a teammate's corpse resurrects them on the
   spot.

Independently, the dead respawn pacifist on a timer (standard respawn
scheduling) — revival before the timer fires consumes the corpse and cancels
the pending respawn (the player path's `live_duplicate_exists` guard already
does this; the same guard is needed for scheduled bots here).

**Can-damage status on the HUD.** Each character's HUD must show whether they
can currently deal damage (armed / pacifist). ModeState only carries 4 global
HUD lines and 4 beacons, so this needs a small engine addition — e.g. a
per-fighter armed flag the score panel renders as an icon next to the
special/weapon readout. Worth doing as a generic "mode status glyph per
fighter" hook rather than Office-only.

**Desk raiding.** Raiders can attack *desks* themselves:
generators-as-workstations with HP; a damaged desk produces nothing until a
worker repairs it by spending work time on it. Gives raids a target other
than bodies.

**Levels.** Three authored levels in the band (e.g. 860-862): one 2-team, one
3-team, one 4-team office floor — team wings (the home-turf zones for the
defense rule), desks per wing, shared corridors, coffee machine(s) placed as
contested neutral ground.

### Open questions

1. Friendly revive vs enemy "finishing": can raiders drag/guard corpses to
   delay revival, or is camping bodies (and intercepting coffee carriers)
   enough counterplay?
2. Does home-turf defense extend to protecting the coffee machine if it sits
   in neutral ground, or is the machine deliberately outside everyone's
   armed zone?
3. Coffee balance: one machine per map (hot contested spot) vs one per wing
   (safe but slower)?

Implemented as an `on_damage` hook zeroing attacker damage when neither condition holds.

title: [Integration]: [.NET SDK] ZVec.NET — First .NET Core SDK for ZVec (alongside Python & Node.js)
body:
### Target Framework

.NET

### Motivation

Hi ZVec team 👋

I've built and published ZVec.NET — the first production .NET SDK for ZVec, bringing full vector database capabilities to the .NET ecosystem alongside your existing Python and Node.js SDKs.

NuGet: [nuget.org/packages/ZVec.NET](https://www.nuget.org/packages/ZVec.NET/)
GitHub: [github.com/ahmedSamir50/AdamSystems.ZVec.NET](https://github.com/ahmedSamir50/AdamSystems.ZVec.NET)
License: MIT (same as ZVec)
Current version: 1.0.0-beta.3.2+zvec.0.5.1 => 1.0.0-beta.4+zvec.0.6.0 build will be launched soon to match the ZVec latest version 0.6.0. 
Why .NET Integration Matters
.NET is a top-5 language ecosystem by developer population — over 7 million active developers worldwide (SlashData 2025). It dominates enterprise, government, banking, and healthcare sectors, where vector search is increasingly critical for AI-powered features. Yet the .NET ecosystem has historically been underserved by vector database vendors, who typically ship Python and Node.js SDKs first and treat .NET as an afterthought.

ZVec.NET changes this by providing a first-class, production-grade .NET SDK that wraps the full zvec_c_api C interface — not a thin P/Invoke wrapper, but a full-featured SDK with typed ODM mapping, DI-first ergonomics, SafeHandle resource safety, and cross-platform native binaries.

Who Benefits
Enterprise .NET developers building AI features (semantic search, RAG pipelines, recommendation engines, anomaly detection) — they get a vector database that runs in-process with no Docker, no network overhead, and no external service dependency. ZVec's in-process architecture (like SQLite) is a natural fit for .NET.
The ZVec project — listing a .NET SDK alongside Python and Node.js signals ecosystem maturity and expands adoption into the enterprise segment, where .NET is dominant. This is the same pattern PostgreSQL (Npgsql), MySQL (Pomelo), and SQLite (SQLitePCLRaw) used to grow their .NET communities.
Edge/mobile developers — ZVec.NET already ships native binaries for android-arm64 and android-x64, with MAUI sample apps demonstrating offline RAG on mobile devices. This is a use case Python and Node.js cannot serve.
The broader AI/ML community — .NET developers building production RAG systems now have a low-latency, zero-dependency vector database option that works on edge devices, in desktop apps (MAUI), and in cloud services (ASP.NET Core) — all from a single NuGet package.
What ZVec.NET Covers
The SDK wraps the full zvec_c_api surface and exposes it as idiomatic C#:
| Feature | Status |
|---------|--------|
| HNSW, Flat, IVF, DiskANN, Vamana, Invert, FTS indexes | ✅ |
| HNSW-RaBitQ (quantized HNSW) — with `PlatformNotSupportedException` gate on ARM | ✅ |
| CRUD (Insert, Update, Upsert, Delete, Fetch) — typed + dynamic | ✅ |
| Single + Multi-vector query with RRF/Weighted rerankers | ✅ |
| Hybrid search (dense + sparse) | ✅ |
| Full-text search (FTS) — Standard, Jieba, Whitespace tokenizers | ✅ |
| Expression filters (typed: `p => p.Category == "x"`) + dynamic filter builder | ✅ |
| Schema evolution (AddColumn, DropColumn, CreateIndex, DropIndex, Optimize) | ✅ |
| Typed ODM via `ZVec.NET.Mapping` — POCO mapping with `[ZVecVector]`, `[ZVecField]`, `[ZVecId]` attributes | ✅ |
| DI integration (ASP.NET Core `AddZVec()` / `AddZVecCollection()`) | ✅ |
| Health checks (`ZVecHealthCheck`) | ✅ |
| Sync + Async APIs with `CancellationToken` | ✅ |
| Cross-platform natives (win-x64, linux-x64, osx-arm64, android-arm64/x64) | ✅ |
| ABI version gate (`zvec_check_version` + major match) | ✅ |
| Sample apps: ASP.NET Minimal API, MAUI Blazor Hybrid (offline RAG), Console | ✅ |

Binding Performance
BenchmarkDotNet results (768-dim Flat, 10k docs, win-x64, native ZVec v0.5.1, .NET 8):
| Metric | .NET (ZVec.NET) | Python | Node.js |
|--------|-----------------|--------|---------|
| Query (10k, topk=10, no vectors) | **2.88 ms** | 4.33 ms | 4.10 ms |
| Warm query (128 docs) | **0.51 ms** | 0.41 ms | 1.59 ms |
| Batch insert (1000 docs) | **~16.8k docs/sec** | ~7.1k docs/sec | ~5.8k docs/sec |

The .NET SDK is competitive with — and in some cases faster than — the official Python and Node.js bindings, thanks to [LibraryImport] source-generated P/Invoke and ReadOnlyMemory<float> pin-based vector pipelines.

### Required Interface

ZVec.NET implements no external framework adapter — it is a standalone SDK that wraps the zvec_c_api C interface directly. The SDK defines its own interface contract:
| Interface | Responsibility |
|-----------|---------------|
| `IZvecFactory` | Process-wide initialization (`Initialize`/`Shutdown`), collection lifecycle (`CreateAndOpen`/`Open`). Implements `IDisposable`, `IAsyncDisposable`. Tracks open collections; `Shutdown` disposes all tracked collections before calling `zvec_shutdown`. |
| `IZvecCollection<T>` | Typed per-collection operations: typed CRUD (Insert/Update/Upsert/Delete/Fetch with POCO mapping), typed Query with expression filters (`p => p.Category == "demo"`), typed DDL (`DropColumnAsync(p => p.Year)`, `CreateIndexAsync(p => p.Year, ...)`). |
| `IZvecCollection` (dynamic) | Dynamic operations via `ZVecDoc`, string field names, `ZVecFilterBuilder`. Accessible from typed collection via `.Untyped`. |

DI Registration (ASP.NET Core / Generic Host / MAUI)
builder.Services.AddZVec(options => { ... });
builder.Services.AddZVecCollection(options => { ... });  // typed
builder.Services.AddZVecCollection("key", options => { ... });  // keyed dynamic
Supports IConfiguration binding (appsettings.json), health checks (AddCheck("zvec")), and keyed services ([FromKeyedServices("products")]).

Interop Contract
The SDK communicates with ZVec exclusively through the zvec_c_api C ABI:

P/Invoke: [LibraryImport("zvec_c_api")] — source-generated marshalling (no runtime reflection).
Handle safety: Collection handles owned by SafeZvecHandle (close-only on Dispose; Destroy deletes on-disk data then closes). ZVecFactory.Shutdown disposes all tracked open collections before calling zvec_shutdown.
Memory model: ReadOnlyMemory<float> on all vector hot paths — pinned via Memory.Pin(), passed as a native pointer, no intermediate float[] copies on the query pin path.
Concurrency: Optional throttles via MaxConcurrentNativeCalls / MaxConcurrentReads (use SemaphoreSlim when > 0; 0 = unlimited). Native ZVec is already thread-safe.
Error handling: All native return codes are mapped to the ZVecErrorCode enum; failures throw ZVecNativeException with native error message extraction via zvec_get_last_error(). ABI gate throws ZVecAbiMismatchException on version mismatch.
Platform gates: PlatformNotSupportedException thrown before native call for HNSW-RaBitQ on ARM (requires x86_64 + AVX2) and DiskANN on non-Linux (requires libaio).
Typed ODM (ZVec.NET.Mapping)
The SDK includes a typed ODM layer that maps POCOs to ZVec collections:
public sealed class Product
{
    public string Id { get; set; } = "";
    public string Title { get; set; } = "";
    public string Category { get; set; } = "";

    [ZVecVector(768, Metric = ZVecMetricType.Cosine, M = 32, EfConstruction = 256)]
    public ReadOnlyMemory<float> Embedding { get; set; }
}

// Schema from POCO
var schema = ZVecCollectionSchemaBuilder.From<Product>().Build();

// Typed query with expression filter
var hits = products.Query(p => p.Embedding, queryVec, topK: 10, filter: p => p.Category == "demo");

No VectorStore Abstraction (Yet)
ZVec.NET does not implement Microsoft.Extensions.VectorData.IVectorStore (the new .NET AI abstraction in preview). This is intentional for v1 — the SDK wraps ZVec's own API surface idiomatically first. A VectorStore adapter can be added in a future version once Microsoft.Extensions.VectorData API stabilizes, and ZVec is officially listed as a supported provider.

### Reference Implementations

Official ZVec SDKs (same C API, different language)
| SDK | Vector DB | Interop | DI | Typed ODM | Mobile RIDs |
|-----|-----------|---------|-----|-----------|-------------|
| [Npgsql](https://github.com/npgsql/npgsql) | PostgreSQL + pgvector | Native P/Invoke | ✅ | EF Core provider | ❌ |
| [Milvus .NET SDK](https://github.com/milvus-io/milvus-sdk-csharp) | Milvus | gRPC | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ |
| [Qdrant Client .NET](https://github.com/qdrant/qdrant-client-csharp) | Qdrant | gRPC | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ |
| [SQLitePCLRaw](https://github.com/ericsink/SQLitePCLRaw) | SQLite | Native P/Invoke | ✅ | ❌ | ✅ |
| **ZVec.NET** | **ZVec** | **Native P/Invoke (`[LibraryImport]`)** | **✅** | **✅ (`ZVec.NET.Mapping`)** | **✅ (Android)** |

ZVec.NET's architecture is most similar to SQLitePCLRaw and Npgsql: native P/Invoke wrapping a C ABI, SafeHandle for resource safety, single NuGet with RID-specific native binaries, and DI-first public API. The key differences are:

In-process (like SQLite) rather than client-server (like PostgreSQL/Milvus/Qdrant) — making native P/Invoke the only appropriate interop strategy.
Typed ODM — a feature Npgsql has via EF Core, but ZVec.NET provides natively via ZVec.NET.Mapping without requiring an ORM.
Mobile RIDs — Android ARM64/x64 native binaries, with MAUI sample apps demonstrating offline edge RAG. This is unique among .NET vector DB SDKs.
Competing NuGet Package
There is another .NET package wrapping ZVec — [Zvec](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Zvec) by TheBitBrine. It provides a thinner sync P/Invoke surface using float[] (not ReadOnlyMemory), covers fewer index types (no RaBitQ, DiskANN, Vamana, FTS), and targets desktop RIDs only. ZVec.NET is the more complete SDK with DI, typed ODM, async, expression filters, and mobile support. Both packages wrap the same zvec_c_api.


Steps I Plan to Follow
✅ Published ZVec.NET on NuGet — 1.0.0-beta.3.2+zvec.0.5.1 ([nuget.org/packages/ZVec.NET](https://www.nuget.org/packages/ZVec.NET/))
✅ Published sample apps: ASP.NET Minimal API, MAUI Blazor Hybrid (offline RAG), Console
✅ Published BenchmarkDotNet results comparing .NET vs Python vs Node.js
✅ Opened this ecosystem integration issue
⬜ Submit a PR to alibaba/zvec adding ZVec.NET to the README's SDK/ecosystem section (if maintainers are open to it)
⬜ Add .NET code examples alongside Python/Node.js in ZVec documentation (if docs accept community contributions)
⬜ Coordinate with maintainers on ABI version pinning strategy for future ZVec releases
⬜ Implement Microsoft.Extensions.VectorData.IVectorStore adapter once the API stabilizes
⬜ Announce on ZVec community channels (Discord/Discussions, if they exist)

title: [Bug]: Windows ARM64 (MSVC): ailego CMake returns early and never creates zvec_ailego
body:
### Description

Configuring zvec for **Windows ARM64 with MSVC** fails at CMake configure (before any compile of `zvec_c_api`).

`src/ailego/CMakeLists.txt` enters the ARM path correctly (`HOST_ARCH` matches `arm|arm64`), then does:

```cmake
elseif (HOST_ARCH MATCHES ^(arm|arm64)$)
    if(MSVC)
        return()
    endif()
    set(MATH_MARCH_FLAG_NEON -march=armv8-a)
    ...
endif()

cc_library(
    NAME zvec_ailego STATIC STRICT PACKED
    ...
)
```

The `return()` exits **this** CMakeLists before `cc_library`, so target `zvec_ailego` is never created.

Meanwhile `src/CMakeLists.txt` still has `BUILD_ZVEC_AILEGO_SHARED=ON` (default) and calls `zvec_add_all_in_one_shared(zvec_ailego_shared ... LIBS zvec_ailego)`, which fatals:

```text
CMake Error at src/CMakeLists.txt:31 (message):
  Target zvec_ailego is required by zvec_ailego_shared
```

So ARM64 itself works for non-MSVC compilers; **MSVC ARM64 is aborted without disabling the shared target that depends on ailego**.

### Contrast (same zvec pin, same CI matrix)

On the same desktop native workflow:

| Target | Compiler | Result |
|--------|----------|--------|
| linux-arm64 | GCC/Clang | success |
| osx-arm64 (Apple Silicon) | AppleClang | success |
| win-arm64 | MSVC | configure FATAL above |

All three hit `HOST_ARCH` arm/arm64; only MSVC hits `return()`.

Public job: https://github.com/ahmedSamir50/AdamSystems.ZVec.NET/actions/runs/30286685888/job/90046139977

### Steps to Reproduce

On Windows with the MSVC arm64 toolset (x64 host → arm64 target is enough; a native Windows ARM MSVC build should hit the same `return()`):

```bat
cmake -B build -G Ninja ^
  -DCMAKE_SYSTEM_NAME=Windows ^
  -DCMAKE_SYSTEM_PROCESSOR=ARM64 ^
  -DBUILD_C_BINDINGS=ON ^
  -DBUILD_ZVEC_AILEGO_SHARED=ON
```

Configure ends with `Target zvec_ailego is required by zvec_ailego_shared`.

Log excerpts from CI:

```text
-- BUILD_ZVEC_AILEGO_SHARED:ON
-- turbo: ARM64 detected, skipping x86-specific optimizations
CMake Error at external/zvec/src/CMakeLists.txt:31 (message):
  Target zvec_ailego is required by zvec_ailego_shared
-- Configuring incomplete, errors occurred!
```

### Suggested fix

1. **Preferred:** Remove the MSVC `return()` and wire MSVC-compatible ARM64 / NEON flags (instead of GCC-style `-march=armv8-a`) so `cc_library(zvec_ailego)` still runs on MSVC ARM64.
2. Or, if MSVC ARM64 ailego is intentionally unsupported for now: emit a clear error and turn off `BUILD_ZVEC_AILEGO_SHARED` / skip `zvec_add_all_in_one_shared` when the static target was not created (do not FATAL after silently skipping the library).

A silent `return()` that leaves the shared graph enabled is what bites consumers.

### Additional Context

- zvec ~**0.5.1** (C bindings / all-in-one shared defaults).
- Hit while packaging the C API for .NET ([AdamSystems.ZVec.NET](https://github.com/ahmedSamir50/AdamSystems.ZVec.NET)); host win64 `protoc` was injected correctly — failure is earlier, in ailego CMake.
- Ruled out binding / runtime teardown (not #619-class): this is configure-only; managed code never runs. Linux and Apple Silicon ARM64 natives on the same matrix are green.
- Happy to test a PR.

### Operating System

Windows (MSVC arm64 toolset; CI: windows-2025 x64 host + amd64→arm64 cross).

### Build & Runtime Environment

- Generator: Ninja
- Compiler: MSVC 19.51.x (`Hostx64/arm64`)
- Flags: `-DCMAKE_SYSTEM_NAME=Windows -DCMAKE_SYSTEM_PROCESSOR=ARM64`, `BUILD_C_BINDINGS=ON`, `BUILD_ZVEC_AILEGO_SHARED=ON`
comments:
Thanks for the report! MSVC ARM64 wasn't supported initially due to a lack of clear use cases, but we now have a community PR (#352) under review to fix the CMake and architecture-macro issues. We hope to merge it soon. 😄 

BTW, do you know of any scenarios, or have you run into any yourself, that require running .NET applications (or zvec) on ARM64?

title: [Bug]: 磁盘随optimize次数线性膨胀
body:
### Description

我在本地试验的时候发现一个奇怪的现象：
假设有3w条数据，全部插入后再进行optmize，则空间是正常的
如果每1w条数据插入一次后进行optmize（之后线上会这么操作，降低锁延迟），则会导致空间膨胀

[cleanup_orphans.py](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/30642346/cleanup_orphans.py)
[parse_manifest.py](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/30642347/parse_manifest.py)
[disk_test.py](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/30642348/disk_test.py)

文件说明：
disk_test.py 是测试用脚本，用于复现
cleanup_orphans.py 是临时用修复脚本，负责移除孤儿段内容（正是导致空间膨胀的主要原因）

**注意，这三个脚本是由AI生成的，但是已经由人工进行核验和检查实际功能，目前测试下来移除孤儿段不会对现有数据造成影响（但不确定是否会有索引未能加载等其他问题）**

## 以下是AI定位的原因：

zvec 是 LSM 式段存储：数据先进内存 writing segment → 攒够后刷成 persist segment → optimize 把 ≥2 个 persist 段合并成 1 个新段。关键问题出在合并后的清理环节：

CollectionImpl::Optimize() 合并后调用 segment_manager_->destroy_segment() 删除旧段。
SegmentImpl::destroy() 只把 need_destroyed_ 置 true，不删任何文件；真正的物理删除在 ~SegmentImpl() 析构函数里才执行（cleanup() → RemoveDirectory）。
实测：被合并的旧段对象析构从未发生（引用生命周期缺陷），旧段目录（含大体积的 .proxima 索引文件）永久残留。
证据链完整：

manifest 版本清单只引用新段 → 逻辑状态完全正确：doc_count=30000、查询正常，只有磁盘被浪费；
残留文件进程退出后依然在、且全程未被占用（可用 DELETE 权限打开）→ 排除了文件锁，锁定"清理从未执行"；
关掉 INT8 量化、关掉 mmap 均复现 → 与量化/mmap 无关，是基础 compact 路径的 bug。
另外两个附加发现：① INT8 量化路径每个段还会额外存一份 FP32 原始向量副本（3 万条 768 维 ≈ 92MB），孤儿段的这份是浪费大头；② Windows 下 coll.destroy() 也偶发清不干净（我测到残留 91~132MB），所以指望 destroy 回收不可靠。

### Steps to Reproduce

```python
1. 运行disk_test.py 即可复现此问题，版本0.6.0
```

### Logs / Stack Trace

```shell

```

### Operating System

Windows 11 25H2

### Build & Runtime Environment

python 3.13,zvec == 0.6.0

### Additional Context

- [x] I've checked `git status` — no uncommitted submodule changes
- [ ] I built with `CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug`
- [ ] This occurs with or without `COVERAGE=ON`
- [ ] The issue involves Python ↔ C++ integration (pybind11)
comments:
@xiaofeng-ling 感谢报告issue! 复现脚本很有用！ 😃 

已在 Windows 和 Linux 上进行对比，确认该问题主要由两种系统不同的文件删除语义导致。
原实现会在 segment 析构期间先调用 `close()`，再通过 `std::filesystem::remove_all()` 删除目录，但 `close()` 没有提前释放 persist store、WAL 等文件句柄或 mmap。
Linux 允许仍被打开或 mmap 的文件被 unlink：目录项会立即消失，实际空间在最后一个引用关闭后释放。因此相同代码在 Linux 上通常能正常清理；Windows 默认不允许删除仍被占用的文件，导致 `remove_all()` 失败，而原实现没有处理该结果，所以旧 segment 目录永久残留。

#676 修复了该问题。
修复后还有遗留一个低概率的外部句柄场景：例如备份或杀毒工具以不包含 `FILE_SHARE_DELETE` 的方式打开 segment 文件，此时 Windows 仍无法立即删除旧目录。所以当外部句柄释放后，遗留目录将在后续重新打开时清理（依赖 #674 的合入）。

title: Crash during Optimize can leak an orphaned segment dir and fail the next segment allocation after recovery
body:
### Description

Since #614, Optimize moves the compacted output to its final numeric
directory and opens it in the lock-free phase, before the manifest is
persisted in the exclusive commit phase:

1. `allocate_segment_id()` returns N (in-memory fetch_add, not persisted)
2. `MoveDirectory(tmp -> <collection>/N)` — numeric dir now exists on disk
3. `Segment::Open(<collection>/N)` — heavy I/O (reads files, builds mmaps)
4. Optimize then waits for the exclusive schema lock; only the commit
   phase persists `next_segment_id = N+1` via version flush

If the process crashes between step 2 and the commit-phase flush,
recovery restores `segment_id_allocator_` from the old manifest (back
to N) and neither opens nor removes the unreferenced directory
`<collection>/N`. After recovery, the first operation that allocates
segment id N fails:

- an Insert that switches the writing segment hits
  `Segment::CreateAndOpen`'s existence check and returns
  "Segment create failed: segment path already exists" to the user;
- a schema DDL switching the writing segment fails the same way;
- the next Optimize fails at `MoveDirectory` (rename onto a non-empty
  directory, ENOTEMPTY).

Since `allocate_segment_id()` is fetch_add, the failure is one-shot
(a retry allocates N+1 and succeeds), but the orphaned directory — a
full compacted segment — is never referenced and never removed, i.e. a
permanent disk leak, and the first user operation after recovery can
spuriously fail.

The pre-#614 code had the same rename-before-flush window, but it was
microseconds wide (rename immediately followed by apply/flush in the
exclusive section). #614 materially widens it: the window now contains
`Segment::Open`'s I/O plus the wait for the exclusive schema lock
(unbounded if long readers hold the shared lock).

Expected: crash recovery leaves the collection in a state where
subsequent operations do not fail due to leftovers of an uncommitted
Optimize, and uncommitted output directories do not leak disk space.
I plan to submit a PR that removes segment directories not referenced
by the recovered manifest (numeric dirs absent from
`persisted_segment_metas()`, plus `*.tmp` residue) during `recovery()`,
where the collection file lock guarantees no concurrent Optimize.

### Steps to Reproduce

```python
1. Build a collection with enough persisted segments that Optimize produces a merged output (CompactTask)
2. Run Optimize() and kill the process after the tmp directory is renamed to its numeric path but before the commit phase flushes the manifest (e.g. inject a sleep/crash right after Segment::Open in the lock-free phase)
3. Reopen the collection (crash recovery), then insert until the writing segment switches, or run Optimize() again
4. The first operation that allocates the orphaned segment id fails; the orphaned numeric directory stays on disk permanently
```

### Logs / Stack Trace

```shell
Segment create failed: segment path already exists [<collection>/N]
move segment directory failed
```

### Operating System

macOS (Apple Silicon M5); applies to all platforms

### Build & Runtime Environment

Apple clang, CMake + Ninja (Homebrew), C++17; found by code inspection on main (post-#614), not platform-specific

### Additional Context

- [x] I've checked `git status` — no uncommitted submodule changes
- [ ] I built with `CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug`
- [ ] This occurs with or without `COVERAGE=ON`
- [ ] The issue involves Python ↔ C++ integration (pybind11)

Optimize then waits for the exclusive schema lock; only the commit phase persists `next_segment_id = N+1` via version flush If the process crashes between step 2 and the commit-phase flush, recovery restores `segment_id_allocator_` from the old manifest (back to N) and neither opens nor removes the unreferenced directory `<collection>/N`.

title: [gfxrecon-convert] Should failed conversions clean up partial output files?
body:
Follow on to pending commit [a0a74256](https://github.com/LunarG/gfxreconstruct/commit/a0a74256e070df39786069af41c875dd551ea991). After error handling in the tool mains is standardized, it seems worth discussing whether failed conversions should also clean up the output file they leave behind.

## The problem

When `gfxrecon-convert` fails during processing, it exits with a non-zero code but leaves a partially-written `.json` file on disk. Depending on when the failure occurs, the file is in one of two states:

1. Syntactically invalid JSON — if the "no API detected" path is hit, `JsonWriter::StartStream` has already written the opening bracket and header object, but `JsonWriter::Destroy` never runs to write the closing bracket. The file fails to parse.
2. Syntactically valid but truncated — if a block read error occurs mid-stream, `Destroy` does run and closes the JSON structure correctly, but the file contains only frames up to the point of failure with no indication that content is missing.

In both cases the file sits at the expected output path and looks like a successful conversion. Any downstream script or CI step that checks for the file's existence rather than the tool's exit code will silently consume incorrect data.

## Question

Is cleaning up partial/invalid output files on failure something the team wants to address as a follow-on to `a0a74256`? Interested in thoughts on whether this is considered a bug worth fixing or acceptable current behavior.
comments: @MarkY-LunarG Commit https://github.com/LunarG/gfxreconstruct/commit/a0a74256e070df39786069af41c875dd551ea991 makes the change to standardize tools to return either `EXIT_SUCCESS` or `EXIT_FAILURE`. It was part of another PR but got dropped from it. Is that, or a similar change, still in the plan?

> When gfxrecon-convert fails during processing

@tpower-amd Is this only relevant for `gfxrecon-convert`? Is there a similar issue with `gfxrecon-optimize` if the optimizer encounters errors?

@davidd-lunarg Great question. `gfxrecon-optimize` and `gfxrecon-compress` both have the same problem. Both `FileOptimizer` and `CompressionConverter` inherit from `FileTransformer`, which opens the output file in `Initialize` and only calls `fclose` in its destructor, but never remove. A partial output file is left on disk if either tool fails mid-processing. Since `FileTransformer` is the shared base for both, the fix could live there (a flag that removes the output on non-successful exit) rather than in each tool's `main`.

`gfxrecon-extract` is different because it writes individual per-shader files rather than a single output, so there's no single artifact to clean up in the same way.
evidence: [gfxrecon-convert] Should failed conversions clean up partial output files?
After error handling in the tool mains is standardized, it seems worth discussing whether failed conversions should also clean up the output file they leave behind.

title: body-parser < 2.3.0 fails open on invalid `limit` (CVE-2026-12590)
body:
## Description

Express depends on `body-parser@^2.2.1`, which resolves to a version affected by
**CVE-2026-12590** (GHSA-v422-hmwv-36x6). body-parser `>=2.0.0 <2.3.0` fails open
when given an invalid `limit` option value — `bytes.parse()` returns `null` and
request body size enforcement is silently disabled, allowing a DoS via oversized
payloads. This is flagged by scanners such as Trivy.

## Expected

`body-parser` resolves to the patched `2.3.0`, which throws on an invalid `limit`
at parser initialization.

## Fix

A fix is proposed in #7390, which bumps the dependency to `body-parser@^2.3.0`.

title: Declare the missing dependencies that packages use
body:
## Description

195 packages in this repository use a package or a system library that they never declare. The checker found 1061 missing entries: 959 `<depend>` and 102 `<test_depend>`.

These packages build today only because another declared dependency re-exports the owner, or because some other package installs the system library. That is luck, not correctness. When an unrelated repository stops re-exporting, the package no longer compiles, and the CI of this repository never sees the change.

- Parent issue: autowarefoundation/autoware#7263
- The same cleanup in `autoware_core` is complete: autowarefoundation/autoware_core#1355

## How each entry was found

The checker uses three kinds of evidence.

- An `#include` of a header, resolved against the package that really ships that header.
- A qualified name such as `rcl_interfaces::msg::ParameterDescriptor` in code, where the header arrives through another dependency. An include scan cannot see this kind.
- A system library such as Boost, Eigen or PCL, resolved through the compiler search paths, `dpkg`, and the rosdep cache, and named by the rosdep key this workspace already prefers.

Comments do not count. The checker blanks comments and string literals before it scans, because a Doxygen example is not a use.

The tag comes from where the dependency is used.

- `<depend>` when the use sits in an installed header or in code compiled into the library. 959 entries.
- `<test_depend>` when only `test/` reaches the dependency. 102 entries.

The checker refuses an entry that would create a dependency cycle. The measurement ran on 2026-08-15, on `main` at 4260f35f2, in a jazzy workspace.

## Validation

These counts are raw checker output. The core rounds reviewed every core entry per package, and the reviews corrected the checker five times. The simulator, e2e and map entries are reviewed, and that review added one entry the checker missed: `tf2` in `tier4_dummy_object_rviz_plugin`. The other components are not reviewed yet.

Each component gets the same per-package review before its pull request, so the counts here can change.

## The entries by component

The most frequent missing dependencies are `libboost-dev` (67), `lanelet2_core` (57), `std_msgs` (57), `geometry_msgs` (55), and `eigen` (54).

| Component | Packages | Entries |
|---|---|---|
| `planning` | 57 | 501 |
| `perception` | 48 | 260 |
| `control` | 19 | 77 |
| `localization` | 12 | 47 |
| `visualization` | 12 | 38 |
| `sensing` | 11 | 37 |
| `common` | 10 | 33 |
| `evaluator` | 6 | 25 |
| `system` | 13 | 21 |
| `vehicle` | 4 | 10 |
| `simulator` | 1 | 5 |
| `e2e` | 1 | 4 |
| `map` | 1 | 3 |
| **Total** | **195** | **1061** |

## Pull requests

One pull request per component, opened one at a time, after its review, smallest first. The three smallest components share one pull request. `planning` is large, and it can split into several pull requests.

- [x] simulator, e2e and map, in one pull request: #13209
- [x] vehicle: #13208
- [ ] system https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/pull/13217

## Definition of done

- Every reviewed entry is present in the `package.xml` of its package, with the tag given.
- A build of the changed packages and their reverse-dependency closure stays clean.

Adding a `<depend>` cannot break a build, so this work carries no risk to the packages themselves.

---

Written with Claude Code. The entries come from the checker that produced the core list, and a per-package review runs before each pull request.
